howExperiencePagesAssemble:

1. Wrapper: src/pages/experiences/<slug>/index.astro (e.g. beach-island-escapes/index.astro:1-20) is 20 lines: it imports ExperienceLayout and the content partial as a raw string (`import Content from "../../../content-pages/experiences__<slug>.html?raw"`), then renders `<ExperienceLayout title description schemaType name hero={{image, eyebrow, headline, sub, ctaPrimary, ctaSecondary:{href:"#destinations"}}}><Fragment set:html={Content} /></ExperienceLayout>`. No pageCss (verifier forbids it, verify-deployment.mjs:101-121).

2. Layout: src/layouts/ExperienceLayout.astro. Imports section-shared.css then experience.css (lines 20-21; order is load-bearing, experience.css overrides .intro-content and .seasons-grid). Props interface lines 25-44 (title, description, ogImage, canonicalPath, schemaType, name, hero). The breadcrumb trail is HARDCODED at lines 51-55: [Home /, Experiences /experiences/, {name}] — there is no parent/region prop, unlike DestinationLayout:44/72. Line 56 `const bodyHtml = await Astro.slots.render("default")` renders the slot once up front; line 57 `extractFaq(bodyHtml)` (schema.ts:269-278) parses `.pf-item` blocks out of that string.

3. Schema: lines 58-68 build an array [breadcrumbs(SITE, trail), webPage(...), service(SITE,{name, serviceType:name, description, path}), faq(pairs)|null] from src/lib/schema.ts (breadcrumbs 119-130, webPage 225-237, service 181-196, faq 243-253). og:image is derived from hero.image via OG_CROPS (src/lib/og-crops.ts, generated by tools/make-og-crops.mjs) at lines 75-79.

4. Markup: Base (src/layouts/Base.astro) receives title/description/ogImage/schema/preloadImage/active="experiences" (lines 82-92). Base.astro:53-58 derives canonical/og:url from Astro.site + Astro.url.pathname (no query string, deliberate), prints JSON-LD through Schema.astro:18-20 (one <script type=application/ld+json> per node), then Header, <main id="main"><slot/></main>, Newsletter, Turnstile, Footer, Accordion, Analytics (148-159). Inside the slot the layout emits .breadcrumb (94-105, rendered from the SAME trail array), the .exp-hero section (107-129), then `<Fragment set:html={bodyHtml} />` (133) — the partial verbatim.

5. Partial: src/content-pages/experiences__<slug>.html (beach-island-escapes.html, 373 lines) in order: intro-section (+ .answer-capsule, line 6), `exp-cards-section id="destinations"` (line 25) holding `.exp-cards.exp-cards--photo` with six (family-travel and food-wine-travel: nine) `<a class="exp-card" href="/plan-your-trip/">` tiles (lines 33-46 shape: exp-card__img with alt/width/height/loading=lazy/decoding, __body > __region/__name/__desc/__tags, __arrow "Explore →"), events-section (108), inclusions-section (165), seasons-strip (197), exp-cta (236), cost-range (251, inserted by tools/p3-8-cost-insert.mjs), page-faq (296, 8 pf-items), read-more (348, 3 journal links). 6. Build (package.json:10): check-node → restore-lockfile → astro build (sitemap integration, lastmod from tools/git-lastmod.mjs:188-211 = last commit touching src/pages/experiences/<slug>/index.astro OR src/content-pages/experiences__<slug>.html) → format-sitemap → strip-internal-comments (drops NEEDS MARK/FIGURE/TODO comments, content-checks.mjs:85-91) → restore-images → build-responsive-images (wraps exp-card__img and exp-hero__img in <picture> with AVIF/WebP, build-responsive-images.mjs:9-14) → verify-checks.test.mjs (fixtures) → verify-deployment.mjs.

existingDataLayer:
There is NO tile→page mapping anywhere today: all 78 .exp-card hrefs are the literal string "/plan-your-trip/" inside the 12 partials, and nothing in tools/, src/lib or docs/ records what each tile is meant to resolve to (grep of docs/ and CLAUDE.md for exp-card/place-card href decisions returns nothing). There is also no src/data/ directory. What DOES exist is a mature \"data file + idempotent insert script\" pattern, used three times:

(1) tools/cost-ranges-data.mjs + tools/p3-8-cost-insert.mjs — the canonical example. The data file is a plain ESM module exporting `VERIFIED` and `COST_RANGES`, an object KEYED BY CONTENT-PARTIAL FILENAME (\"destinations__africa.html\", \"experiences__cruises.html\"), 80 rows, each `{range|noBand+unit, includes[], excludes[], drivers[], source:{text, href}, verified?}` (header lines 1-57 explain the two row shapes and warn that hand-counted totals in the header rotted twice). The insert script (p3-8-cost-insert.mjs) reads each row, locates the page's commented scaffold with a tolerant regex `BLOCK` (line 45, accepts two terminator forms because the first version silently skipped 20 of 22 pages), checks `isLive()` on a comment-stripped copy (line 50), HTML-escapes every field (esc, 52-54), refuses non-https hrefs and comment terminators (56-59, 62-64), renders the section from a template literal, `html.replace(block, () => section)` (function form so `$` in data is not interpreted), writes with utf8, and prints DERIVED counts (229-240). Idempotent: already-live pages are skipped. Safety is then re-verified in dist by the inert-cost-section / unsafe-href / cost-figure-shape checks, with fixtures.

(2) tools/p3-6-related-destinations.mjs — data INLINE in the script: `DEST` (slug → [display name, region label, hub slug, hero image], lines 32-97) and `RELATED` (slug → three sibling slugs, 100-162). It renders three .related-card anchors with rc- crops derived from the hero path (`cardCrop`, 174-175, CROP_W/H 760x435 matching make-related-card-crops.mjs), and inserts the block BEFORE `<section class=\"page-faq\">` (FAQ_OPEN, 165, 232-233), or REWRITES IN PLACE when a `data-p3-6` section already exists (226-230) — the comment at 219-225 explains why rewrite-not-skip matters. This DEST map is the closest thing to a destination registry and is also what make-related-card-crops.mjs reads.

(3) tools/exp-card-intake.mjs / place-card-intake.mjs — image intake that rewrites card markup in the partial, writes public/assets/img + images-b64 twin + MANIFEST through tools/image-manifest.mjs, and gates the --photo modifier.

Other data files: tools/itin-brief.json (itinerary image briefs: id/family/file/w/h/alt/prompt — image generation, not page data), tools/image-manifest.json and image-gen-manifest-*.json (image generation briefs), images-b64/MANIFEST.json (1,216 entries {b64, target, bytes}, sorted by target, indent-1 LF), images-b64/ALIASES.json (11 legacy /assets/<name>.jpg → /assets/img/ canonical). The hub ItemLists are discovered by `import.meta.glob(\"./*/index.astro\")` plus hand NAME maps (experiences/index.astro:12-50, destinations/index.astro:13-29) — direct children only. Precedent for a src-side import of a tools module exists (astro.config.mjs:3 imports ./tools/git-lastmod.mjs), so a data module can be imported by both Astro and node tools provided it is plain .mjs (a .ts file is not loadable by the node tools without a loader).

Shape: `export const TILES = { "experiences__beach-island-escapes.html": [ { name: "Maldives", href: "/destinations/maldives/", note: "country page" }, { name: "Turks & Caicos", href: "/destinations/turks-caicos/" }, ... ] }` — keyed by partial filename like COST_RANGES, rows in DOCUMENT ORDER with the tile's exact `exp-card__name` text so the inserter can refuse on mismatch; `href` may carry a fragment only from an allowed set (#places, #experiences, #seasons…); `note` records editorial intent (hub, journal post, new page pending).

Destination pages consume the reverse index by importing the same module in DestinationLayout (`featuredIn(path)` helper exported from tiles.mjs: groups rows by href pathname with fragment stripped) and rendering the FeaturedIn component at the marker (see enhancement mechanics). Broken/inconsistent links are prevented by (1) the inserter's name/count refusal, (2) existing internal-links dead-href check, (3) new `exp-card-targets` check: no .exp-card href equals /plan-your-trip/ (or any href in a small allowlist) and every href is a same-site path, (4) new `card-fragment-resolves` check, (5) new `tile-map-parity` check reading src/content-pages against the map so the partial and the map cannot drift, (6) `featured-in-parity` for the reverse links.
